chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has dirhams (a debt) upon another man, so he gifts them to him. Is it for him to retract from it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq.
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمُ: Dirhams (silver coins), used here to represent a monetary debt.
key_terms.يَرْجِعَ: To retract or take back (the gift).
key_terms.يَهَبُهَا: He gifts it (the act of giving a gift/hibah).

ai.seo_question: Can a creditor retract a gift of debt to the debtor?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when a creditor gifts the debt amount to the debtor, it constitutes a final transfer of ownership (*hibah*), rendering it irrevocable. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between settling a debt via gift versus other forms of debt forgiveness, emphasizing the creditor's intent to permanently relinquish the claim. The hadith underscores the principle that once the gift is accepted and possession is established, the right of revocation (*ruju'*) no longer applies.
